newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares get boost but lack clear direction.
newsitem.headline: German shares get boost but lack clear direction.

text.p: German shares maintained gains in post-bourse IBIS dealings on Thursday, getting a boost from a slightly firmer dollar which helped to dampen the impact of Wednesday's sharp drop on Wall Street.
At 1500 GMT, the IBIS DAX was up 16.64 points at 2,853.00 points and slightly above the bourse DAX index at 2,847.08, which was up 6.03 points for the day.
But traders said the market still lacked clear direction and was following U.S. market movements and the general uncertainity gripping world financial markets.
"The German market is not able to move on its own for the moment and is relying on Wall Street for help," said one Frankfurt trader said.

Dealers said the firmer dollar, which was trading at about 1.540 marks in European dealings on Thursday, was largely responsible for boosting the market after falling with the U.S. in after-hours market trading on Wednesday.
The dollar was particularly helpful for export-sensitive shares, including chemicals and carmaker stocks.
Chemical group Hoechst AG ended bourse trade up 2.43 marks at 73.28 marks, while Bayer AG was up 56 pfennigs at 62.65 marks.
But electronics group Siemens AG ended down 65 pfennigs at 72.55 marks after a slew of mixed news, which some dealers thought was positive, although others disagreed.

Shipmaker Bremer Vulkan, once Germany's biggest shipyard, was the session's top loser, closing down 35 pfennigs at two marks as the bankrupt company said on Wednesday it had only enough money to keep its flagship yard open through year-end.
